articleHtml:
Via 313 Nutrition Calculator

Via 313 is built around Detroit-style pizza, and that changes how I would calculate a meal compared with a typical thin-crust pizza restaurant.

A Detroit-style slice has a thick, airy crust, cheese that reaches the edges, and substantial toppings. A single square can therefore contain more calories, fat, protein, and sodium than its size might suggest.

The Via 313 Nutrition Calculator helps you look beyond the size of the slice. Use it to compare pizzas, calculate several slices, add appetizers or salads, and estimate the nutrition of your complete meal.

You can review calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, sodium, saturated fat, fiber, and other available nutrition values before deciding what fits your meal.

Why Detroit-Style Pizza Needs a Per-Slice Calculator

Pizza nutrition can be difficult to estimate by sight.

A large thin slice can sometimes contain fewer calories than a smaller-looking square of Detroit-style pizza because the thickness, cheese, crust, meat, and toppings differ.

That makes the serving definition important.

Via 313 publishes pizza nutrition on a per-slice basis, so the easiest way to estimate your meal is:

Nutrition per slice × number of slices eaten

If one slice contains 330 calories and you eat two:

330 × 2 = 660 calories

If you eat three:

330 × 3 = 990 calories

The same calculation applies to protein, carbohydrates, fat, and sodium.

This is much more useful than trying to estimate the calories from the physical size of your plate.

One Slice Can Be a Substantial Portion

A Detroit-style pizza is not the type of pizza where I would automatically assume that one slice is a small amount of food.

The thick crust and edge-to-edge cheese make each square relatively dense.

Depending on the recipe and toppings, one slice can provide several hundred calories before you add:

  • Another slice
  • Cheese bread
  • Meatballs
  • Salad dressing
  • Soda
  • Dessert
  • Dipping sauces

That does not mean you need to stop at one slice.

It simply means counting the number of slices gives you a much more realistic estimate of your meal.

Detroit-Style vs Bar-Style Pizza

Via 313 currently serves both Detroit-style and bar-style pizza.

They should not be treated as nutritionally interchangeable.

Detroit-style pizza has a thicker crust and characteristic cheesy edges.

Bar-style pizza is thinner, with a crisp and chewy crust.

Even when the topping combination has a similar name, the different crust and preparation can change calories, carbohydrates, fat, and other nutrition values.

If you are choosing between the two styles, make sure you select the exact version you order.

Do not use the Detroit-style nutrition value for a bar-style slice or vice versa.

Start With the Pizza Style

A useful way to calculate your meal is to make decisions in this order:

First, choose between Detroit-style and bar-style pizza.

Second, choose the pizza recipe.

Third, decide how many slices you expect to eat.

Fourth, add appetizers, salads, drinks, sauces, or desserts.

This approach prevents one of the most common pizza-tracking mistakes: entering one slice when you actually ate several.

Classic Cheese Gives You a Useful Baseline

Cheese pizza is useful as a comparison point because it shows what the crust, sauce, and cheese contribute before meat or specialty toppings enter the picture.

When comparing two Via 313 pizzas, start with Classic Cheese and then look at what additional toppings do to:

  • Calories
  • Protein
  • Total fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium
  • Carbohydrates

Adding meat may increase protein, but it can also increase calories, fat, and sodium.

Adding vegetables can change the nutrition differently.

This is more useful than assuming every pizza slice has roughly the same numbers.

Pepperoni Changes More Than Protein

Pepperoni is one of the most popular pizza toppings, but it does more than add protein.

It also contributes fat, saturated fat, and sodium.

Via 313 offers pizzas that use different types and amounts of pepperoni, so two pepperoni-based pizzas can have different nutrition profiles.

The Original Pepperoni and The Detroiter, for example, are not the same pizza.

The Detroiter combines smoked pepperoni under the cheese with natural casing pepperoni on top, which creates a different topping load.

If sodium or saturated fat matters to you, compare the full nutrition profile rather than checking protein alone.

The Detroiter Is More Than a Basic Pepperoni Pizza

The Detroiter is one of Via 313's signature pizzas.

Because it combines two pepperoni preparations with Detroit-style crust and cheese, it is more substantial than a simple cheese slice.

When calculating it, pay particular attention to:

  • Number of slices
  • Calories per slice
  • Protein per slice
  • Fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium

If you eat two slices, double all of those values.

If you eat three, multiply by three.

Per-slice nutrition makes that calculation straightforward.

Meat-Heavy Pizzas Can Raise Protein and Calories Together

Via 313 offers several pizzas built around multiple meats.

The Carnivore is a clear example, combining ingredients such as pepperoni, ham, sausage, and bacon.

A meat-heavy pizza can provide more protein than a simple cheese or vegetable pizza, but the additional meat may also raise:

  • Calories
  • Total fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium

If your goal is higher protein, do not automatically choose the pizza with the largest amount of meat.

Compare how much additional protein you receive relative to the increase in calories.

Sometimes a simpler pizza already provides enough protein for your meal.

Vegetable Pizza Is Not Automatically Low Calorie

The Herbivore includes vegetables such as mushroom, onion, green pepper, and black olives.

Those toppings can add flavor, volume, and some nutrients without the same meat contribution as pepperoni or sausage.

However, the pizza still contains Detroit-style crust and cheese.

That means the word "vegetarian" does not automatically mean low calorie.

This applies across restaurant menus.

A useful nutrition comparison should look at the complete recipe rather than judging a food from one topping category.

Marinara Is Structurally Different

The Marinara is particularly different from many other Via 313 Detroit-style pizzas because it does not use cheese in the standard recipe.

That can substantially change its calorie, fat, saturated fat, and protein profile.

If you are comparing Via 313 pizzas for lower calories or dairy avoidance, it is worth reviewing separately rather than grouping it with cheese-based pizzas.

However, customizations can change the final result.

Always calculate the version you actually order.

Specialty Pizzas Can Hide Significant Differences

Some of Via 313's specialty pizzas combine ingredients you might not see on a basic pizza.

Examples can include:

  • Prosciutto
  • Gorgonzola
  • Fig preserves
  • Balsamic glaze
  • Hot honey
  • Bacon
  • Cream cheese
  • Pineapple
  • Ricotta
  • Multiple types of pepperoni
  • Sausage
  • Parmesan

A specialty pizza may therefore contain calories from more than crust, sauce, cheese, and meat.

Sweet sauces and preserves can increase carbohydrates and sugar.

Extra cheeses can increase fat and saturated fat.

Cured meats can contribute substantial sodium.

This is why the exact pizza name matters when using the calculator.

The Cadillac Has a Different Nutrition Profile From Pepperoni Pizza

The Cadillac combines ingredients such as prosciutto, Gorgonzola, Parmesan, fig preserves, and balsamic glaze.

That creates a very different balance from a basic pepperoni or cheese pizza.

It contains savory, fatty, and sweet components in the same slice.

If you are comparing it with another pizza, look beyond calories.

Check carbohydrates, fat, saturated fat, protein, and sodium as well.

Two slices with similar calories can still have very different nutrient profiles.

Hot Honey Still Counts

Via 313 uses hot honey on some specialty pizzas.

It may look like a finishing drizzle, but it still contributes to the finished food.

Honey primarily adds carbohydrates and sugar.

If you order a pizza that includes hot honey, calculate the prepared menu item rather than estimating only the crust, cheese, and meat.

The same rule applies to balsamic glaze, fig preserves, ranch drizzle, Buffalo sauce, and other specialty toppings.

Cheese Can Be One of the Biggest Variables

Via 313 is known for cheese reaching the edges of its Detroit-style crust.

Cheese contributes:

  • Calories
  • Protein
  • Fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium

Pizzas with additional cheese varieties can therefore differ from a standard cheese pizza.

The Four Cheese and other cheese-heavy specialty pizzas should be calculated as their own items rather than treated as ordinary cheese pizza.

If you add extra cheese, remember that the customization also changes the final nutrition.

What About Gluten-Free Crust?

Via 313 currently offers a gluten-free vegan crust option for Detroit-style pizzas.

Gluten-free does not automatically mean lower calorie.

A gluten-free crust can still contain substantial carbohydrates and calories.

People sometimes choose gluten-free food expecting it to be lighter, but gluten content and calorie content are separate issues.

Choose the gluten-free version when it fits your dietary needs or preference, then check its nutrition separately.

Gluten-Free Is Especially Important for Allergy Awareness

Via 313 offers gluten-free options, but people with severe allergies or medically necessary gluten avoidance should pay attention to restaurant preparation practices.

A restaurant kitchen can handle wheat-containing dough alongside gluten-free products.

For someone choosing gluten-free as a preference, that may not be a concern.

For someone with celiac disease or a severe allergy, cross-contact can be much more important than the calorie number.

Nutrition information and allergen safety answer different questions.

Dairy-Free Cheese Changes the Recipe

Dairy-free cheese is another available customization for many Via 313 pizzas.

Like gluten-free crust, dairy-free does not automatically mean low calorie or low fat.

Plant-based cheese products can still contribute significant calories and fat.

If you choose dairy-free cheese, use nutrition information for the customized item when available rather than assuming it has the same values as the standard pizza.

Bar-Style Pizza Gives You Another Way to Adjust the Meal

Via 313's bar-style menu offers a thinner crust.

Current choices include pizzas such as:

  • Plain
  • Plain with Pepperoni
  • MC5
  • Funkadelic Chicken
  • The Supreme(s)
  • The Temptation(s)
  • The Stooges
  • The Continental

Because the crust style differs from Detroit-style pizza, the nutrition per slice can also differ.

This gives you another useful comparison.

Rather than asking only, "Which topping should I choose?" you can also ask, "Which pizza style works better for the meal I want?"

Thin Crust Does Not Automatically Mean Low Calorie

A thinner crust can reduce the amount of dough in a slice, but toppings still matter.

A bar-style pizza loaded with bacon, sausage, pepperoni, multiple cheeses, ranch, or other rich ingredients can still contain substantial calories.

The crust is only one part of the equation.

When comparing styles, consider the complete pizza.

Calculate Two Slices Before You Order

Two slices is a common pizza meal, so it helps to look at the doubled numbers before ordering.

Suppose one slice contains:

350 calories
17 grams protein
34 grams carbohydrates
18 grams fat
750 milligrams sodium

Two slices would provide approximately:

700 calories
34 grams protein
68 grams carbohydrates
36 grams fat
1,500 milligrams sodium

This example shows why multiplication matters.

A per-slice sodium number may look manageable until several slices are combined.

Three Slices Can Change the Picture Quickly

Now consider three slices of the same example:

1,050 calories
51 grams protein
102 grams carbohydrates
54 grams fat
2,250 milligrams sodium

Again, that does not mean three slices are automatically inappropriate.

The purpose of the calculator is to show you the total so you can decide how it fits into the rest of your day.

Sodium Deserves Special Attention With Pizza

Pizza can contain significant sodium from several ingredients at once.

Common sources include:

  • Cheese
  • Pepperoni
  • Sausage
  • Bacon
  • Ham
  • Cured meats
  • Sauce
  • Dough
  • Ranch
  • Gorgonzola
  • Parmesan

One slice may already contain several hundred milligrams of sodium.

When you eat two or three slices plus an appetizer, the total can rise quickly.

If sodium matters to you, calculate the complete meal rather than focusing only on calories.

Appetizers Can Add Another Pizza-Sized Portion of Calories

Via 313 serves appetizers in addition to pizza.

Current choices can include:

  • Cheese Bread
  • Meatballs with Marinara
  • Roasted Broccoli and Cauliflower
  • Roasted Artichokes
  • Brussels Sprouts
  • Detroit Duo

Some are designed for sharing.

This makes portion estimation important.

If four people share an appetizer relatively evenly, you may eat about one quarter of the listed serving.

If two people share it, your portion may be closer to half.

The calculator gives you the full nutrition value. Your job is to estimate how much of it you personally ate.

Cheese Bread Is Easy to Treat as "Just a Starter"

Cheese bread can contribute a substantial amount of calories, carbohydrates, fat, and sodium before the pizza arrives.

If you eat cheese bread plus several slices of pizza, calculate both.

Do not treat the appetizer as nutritionally invisible simply because everyone shared it.

Even a partial serving still contributes to the meal.

Detroit Duo Is Designed for Sharing

The Detroit Duo combines cheese bread styles and dipping sauces.

It can also be customized with toppings.

That means the final nutrition depends not only on how much you eat but also on:

  • Which toppings you choose
  • How much sauce you use
  • How many people share it

If accurate tracking matters, estimate your portion rather than entering the full appetizer when you only ate part of it.

Meatballs Can Be a Higher-Protein Appetizer

Meatballs provide more protein than many bread-based starters, but they can also contribute significant fat and sodium.

Crostini, marinara, and any additional meatballs can increase the total further.

If you order extra meatballs, make sure your calculation reflects the extra portion.

A Salad Is Not Always the Lowest-Calorie Item

Via 313 currently offers salads such as:

  • House
  • Caesar
  • Beet
  • Arugula
  • Antipasto

It is tempting to assume that any salad must contain fewer calories than every slice of pizza.

That is not always a useful assumption.

Cheese, dressing, candied nuts, meat, croutons, and other toppings can significantly change salad nutrition.

For example, an antipasto salad includes meats and cheese, while a Caesar salad includes Parmesan, croutons, and dressing.

Calculate the prepared salad rather than lettuce alone.

Salad Dressing Matters

Dressings can contribute a substantial portion of a salad's:

  • Calories
  • Fat
  • Sodium

If dressing is served separately, the amount you actually use may differ from the standard nutrition serving.

Using half of the dressing can change your estimate.

Using additional dressing can increase it.

If you are comparing two salads, pay attention to the dressing as well as the vegetables.

Pizza Plus Salad Can Be Easier to Portion

One practical strategy is combining a slice or two of pizza with a salad.

This does not automatically make the meal better or worse.

It simply gives you another way to distribute the total amount of food.

For example, you might compare:

Three slices of pizza

with

Two slices plus a House Salad

The second meal may provide more vegetables and volume while creating a different calorie and macro total.

Use the calculator to see the actual difference.

The Lunch Combo Needs a Complete Calculation

Via 313 offers lunch options at participating times and locations.

A two-slice lunch combination may include:

  • Two slices of pizza
  • A small salad
  • A fountain drink

That means the nutrition is not just the two slices.

Add all three parts if you consume them.

Choosing unsweetened tea instead of a regular soda can produce a very different carbohydrate and sugar total.

Choosing a different salad can also change the meal.

Drinks Can Be the Simplest Adjustment

A regular fountain soda adds calories and sugar without much protein or fiber.

Unsweetened tea contributes very little energy.

If you enjoy the same pizza either way, changing the beverage can alter the total meal without changing the food.

This is often one of the easiest comparisons to make in the calculator.

Desserts Can Be Substantial

Via 313's dessert menu can include items such as:

  • Boston Cooler
  • Cinnamon Sticks
  • Superman Ice Cream
  • Hub Cap cookies with ice cream
  • Hub Cap Trio

These are separate foods and should be calculated separately from the pizza.

A dessert can sometimes add as many calories as another slice or more, depending on the item and serving size.

If you plan to have dessert, include it while looking at the meal total rather than adding it mentally afterward.

A Shared Dessert Still Counts

Just like appetizers, dessert is often shared.

If two people split an item evenly, estimate half.

If four people divide it, estimate roughly one quarter.

You do not need laboratory-level precision.

A reasonable portion estimate is far better than counting nothing.

How to Find a Lower-Calorie Via 313 Meal

There is no single order that everyone needs to choose.

Instead, focus on the largest decisions.

You could compare:

  • Detroit-style with bar-style
  • Cheese with meat-heavy pizzas
  • One slice with two slices
  • Two slices with three
  • Pizza alone with pizza plus an appetizer
  • Regular soda with unsweetened tea
  • Full appetizer with a shared portion
  • Standard cheese with dairy-free cheese
  • Standard crust with gluten-free crust

These changes have a much larger effect than worrying about tiny amounts of low-calorie vegetables.

How to Build a Higher-Protein Via 313 Meal

Pizza already contains protein from cheese and, depending on the recipe, meat.

Meat-heavy pizzas can provide more protein, but they may also increase calories, fat, and sodium.

When comparing pizzas for protein, use two numbers:

Total protein per slice

and

Calories per slice

Then multiply both by the number of slices you plan to eat.

You may find that two slices already provide a substantial amount of protein without needing the pizza with the highest possible meat content.

Do Not Judge Protein Efficiency by the Name

A pizza called Carnivore sounds like the obvious high-protein option.

It may indeed provide substantial protein.

But if another pizza provides slightly less protein with significantly fewer calories, that may give you a different protein-to-calorie ratio.

Neither choice is universally better.

The calculator simply gives you enough information to decide what matters for your goals.

What About Carbohydrates?

Most pizza carbohydrates come from the crust, although certain toppings and sauces can contribute additional carbohydrates.

Examples include:

  • Dough
  • Pineapple
  • Fig preserves
  • Honey
  • Balsamic glaze
  • Sweet sauces

A thick Detroit-style crust generally contributes substantially to the carbohydrate total.

If you are tracking carbohydrates, count every slice you eat.

Eating three slices means consuming roughly three times the carbohydrate value shown for one slice.

Fat Can Come From Several Layers

Via 313 pizza can contain fat from:

  • Cheese
  • Pepperoni
  • Sausage
  • Bacon
  • Prosciutto
  • Gorgonzola
  • Ricotta
  • Ranch
  • Olive oil
  • Other toppings

This is why two pizzas with similar carbohydrate totals can still have very different calorie values.

Fat provides more calories per gram than protein or carbohydrates, so topping choices can have a noticeable effect.

Saturated Fat Is Worth Checking Separately

Total fat and saturated fat are not the same value.

Pizza containing substantial cheese, pepperoni, sausage, bacon, and other animal-based ingredients can contain meaningful amounts of saturated fat.

If saturated fat is something you monitor, check the per-slice value and multiply it by your actual portion.

This is especially important when eating several slices.

How to Use the Via 313 Nutrition Calculator

Start by searching for the exact pizza or menu item you plan to eat.

For pizza, confirm whether the value represents:

Detroit-style or bar-style

and make sure the nutrition is listed per slice.

Next, choose how many slices you expect to eat.

Then add any appetizer, salad, drink, dipping sauce, or dessert you plan to have.

Review the combined totals for available nutrients such as:

  • Calories
  • Protein
  • Carbohydrates
  • Total fat
  • Saturated fat
  • Sodium
  • Fiber
  • Sugar
  • Cholesterol

If the total is different from what you expected, change one part of the meal and compare again.

A Simple Example of Building a Pizza Meal

Imagine you plan to have:

Two slices of Detroit-style pizza
A portion of cheese bread
A regular soda

Calculate the two slices first.

Then add the amount of cheese bread you expect to eat.

Finally, add the beverage.

Now compare that meal with:

Two slices
A House Salad
Unsweetened tea

The meals may feel similarly substantial at the table while having very different calorie, carbohydrate, fat, sodium, and sugar totals.

That is the real value of a meal calculator.

It lets you compare complete meals, not isolated foods.

Nutrition Information Disclaimer

Via 313 nutrition values should be treated as estimates based on published restaurant information and standard menu preparation.

Actual nutrition may vary because of portion size, ingredient quantities, substitutions, preparation methods, regional menu differences, recipe updates, toppings, sauces, and other customizations.

Pizza nutrition is especially sensitive to portion size. Make sure you multiply per-slice values by the number of slices you actually consume.

Gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian, and dairy-free menu labels should not be treated as guarantees against allergen cross-contact. Anyone with celiac disease, severe food allergies, or medically necessary dietary restrictions should confirm current preparation and allergen information directly with the restaurant.

Use the calculator as a practical tool for comparing menu choices and estimating your meal rather than as an exact measurement or substitute for individualized medical nutrition advice.

faqs.q: How many calories are in a slice of Via 313 pizza?
faqs.a: Calories vary by pizza recipe and style. Detroit-style, bar-style, cheese, pepperoni, meat-heavy, vegetable, and specialty pizzas can all have different calorie values. Use the exact per-slice entry for the pizza you order.

faqs.q: Are Via 313 nutrition facts listed per slice?
faqs.a: Via 313 publishes pizza nutrition on a per-slice basis. Multiply the per-slice numbers by the number of slices you eat to estimate your meal.

faqs.q: How do I calculate two slices?
faqs.a: Multiply the nutrition value for one slice by two. If one slice contains 350 calories, two contain approximately 700 calories.

faqs.q: How do I calculate three slices?
faqs.a: Multiply every per-slice value by three. This applies to calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, and sodium.

faqs.q: Is Via 313 Detroit-style pizza high in calories?
faqs.a: Detroit-style pizza can be calorie-dense because it combines a thick crust with edge-to-edge cheese and toppings. The exact amount depends on the pizza and number of slices.

faqs.q: Is bar-style pizza lower in calories?
faqs.a: Bar-style pizza uses a thinner crust and can have different nutrition from Detroit-style pizza, but toppings still matter. Compare the exact pizzas rather than assuming every thin-crust option is lower in calories.

faqs.q: Which Via 313 pizza has the most protein?
faqs.a: Meat-heavy pizzas can provide substantial protein, but the exact values depend on the recipe and serving. Compare protein together with calories, fat, saturated fat, and sodium.

faqs.q: Is cheese pizza lower in calories than pepperoni?
faqs.a: A basic cheese pizza can be lower in calories than some pepperoni or multi-meat pizzas, but the exact difference depends on pizza style, serving size, and recipe.

faqs.q: Is The Detroiter the same as regular pepperoni pizza?
faqs.a: No. The Detroiter uses both smoked pepperoni under the cheese and natural casing pepperoni on top, making it a different recipe from The Original Pepperoni.

faqs.q: Does Via 313 have vegetarian pizza?
faqs.a: Yes. Current vegetarian options include pizzas such as Classic Cheese, The Herbivore, Four Cheese, and other applicable menu choices.

faqs.q: Does Via 313 have vegan pizza?
faqs.a: The Marinara is offered without cheese and is identified as a vegan option on the current menu. Vegan crust and dairy-free cheese options may also allow additional customization.

faqs.q: Does Via 313 have gluten-free pizza?
faqs.a: Yes. Via 313 currently offers a gluten-free vegan crust for Detroit-style pizzas.

faqs.q: Is Via 313 gluten-free pizza lower in calories?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Gluten-free refers to the absence of gluten, not to calorie content. Check the nutrition for the specific crust and toppings.

faqs.q: Does Via 313 offer dairy-free cheese?
faqs.a: Yes. Dairy-free cheese is available for applicable pizzas on the current menu.

faqs.q: Is dairy-free cheese lower in calories?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Dairy-free cheese can still contain significant calories and fat. Compare the specific nutrition values rather than assuming it is lighter.

faqs.q: Are Via 313 salads low in calories?
faqs.a: It depends on the salad. Dressing, cheese, meat, nuts, croutons, and other ingredients can make a substantial difference.

faqs.q: Are Via 313 appetizers meant for sharing?
faqs.a: Several appetizers are suitable for sharing. If you eat only part of an appetizer, estimate your portion rather than counting the entire order.

faqs.q: How do I calculate shared cheese bread?
faqs.a: Estimate what fraction of the order you ate. If four people shared it equally, approximately one quarter of the full nutrition values would represent your portion.

faqs.q: Does Via 313 pizza contain a lot of sodium?
faqs.a: Pizza can contain substantial sodium from cheese, dough, sauce, cured meats, and other toppings. Eating several slices increases sodium proportionally, so review the complete meal total.

faqs.q: Can I calculate a whole Via 313 meal?
faqs.a: Yes. Add your pizza slices, appetizer, salad, beverage, dessert, and other available items to estimate the nutrition of the complete meal.
